meta.notes: [bulk-tag pass: added `ccnp-security` tag to 60 questions] [ccnp-security batch 1: 3 balanced rewrites — recall=0]

questions.question: A financial services company is designing an IPsec site-to-site VPN between two data centers. The security team requires Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) so that a future compromise of the pre-shared key cannot decrypt previously captured traffic. Which IKEv2 configuration element enforces PFS on every rekey?
options: Lifetime reduction on the IKEv2 SA to 3600 seconds
A stronger encryption algorithm such as AES-256-GCM in the IKEv2 proposal
Enabling dead peer detection (DPD) on both peers
A Diffie-Hellman group specified in the IPsec (Phase 2) proposal
questions.explanation: PFS is achieved by performing a fresh Diffie-Hellman exchange during each IPsec SA rekey. Configuring a DH group in the IPsec proposal (Phase 2) forces that new exchange, so even if long-term keys are later compromised, previously recorded sessions cannot be decrypted. Stronger ciphers, short lifetimes, and DPD do not by themselves guarantee PFS.

questions.question: An engineer is hardening the control plane of a core Cisco IOS-XE router. Traffic destined to the router itself (routing protocol updates, SSH, SNMP) must be rate-limited and classified so that a flood of ICMP does not exhaust CPU. Which feature should be configured?
options: Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding (uRPF) in strict mode
Hardware-based ACL on each ingress interface denying ICMP
Control Plane Policing (CoPP) with a service-policy applied to
Storm Control on uplink interfaces with ICMP threshold
questions.explanation: CoPP classifies traffic punted to the route processor into policy classes (routing, management, monitoring, undesirable) and applies rate-limiters so that floods of any single class cannot starve legitimate control-plane traffic. uRPF addresses source spoofing, ACLs do not rate-limit, and Storm Control is a Layer 2 feature on data-plane interfaces.

questions.question: A security architect wants to prevent rogue DHCP servers on an access switch and also stop ARP spoofing between hosts in the same VLAN. Which combination of features must be enabled?
options: Port-security sticky with DHCP option 82 insertion
IP Source Guard on access ports with static ARP entries for gateways
BPDU Guard on all access ports and Root Guard on uplinks
questions.explanation: DHCP snooping builds a binding table of legitimate IP-to-MAC-to-port mappings and blocks DHCP server responses on untrusted ports. DAI then validates ARP packets against that binding table, dropping gratuitous ARP spoofs. IP Source Guard complements this by filtering data traffic, but DAI is the specific ARP inspection feature. plus Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) referencing the snooping binding table

questions.question: An enterprise is deploying Cisco ISE 3.x in a distributed architecture with two Policy Administration Nodes (PAN), two Monitoring nodes (MnT), and six Policy Service Nodes (PSN) across two data centers. Which statement about the PAN role is correct?
options: Both PAN nodes are active simultaneously and replicate policy changes bi-directionally
PANs provide RADIUS authentication services directly to network devices
Any PSN can be promoted to PAN automatically if both PANs fail
Only the primary PAN accepts configuration changes;.
questions.explanation: In ISE, only the primary PAN is writeable. The secondary PAN receives replicated configuration and becomes writeable only after a failover (manual, or auto-failover if configured). PSNs handle RADIUS/authentication, not PANs, and PSNs cannot be auto-promoted to PAN. the secondary PAN is a warm standby promoted manually or via auto-failover

questions.question: A network engineer is configuring 802.1X on Cisco Catalyst switches. Corporate laptops authenticate with EAP-TLS using machine certificates, while IP phones and printers lack 802.1X supplicants. The switch port must try 802.1X first and then fall back to MAB if no EAPOL response is received. Which command accomplishes this ordering?
options: dot1x pae authenticator with mab enabled
authentication event no-response action authorize vlan 99
authentication order dot1x mab followed by
questions.explanation: The authentication order command controls which method is tried first; authentication priority controls which can preempt an existing session. Setting both to dot1x-then-mab guarantees 802.1X is attempted first and MAB is used only if the endpoint does not respond to EAPOL. Host-mode and event commands do not control method order.

questions.question: A company wants to enforce user-based segmentation without rewriting ACLs on every switch. Users are tagged at ingress based on their ISE authorization policy, and enforcement decisions are made at egress switches using those tags. Which technology provides this model?
options: Cisco TrustSec with Security Group Tags (SGT) and SGACLs
Private VLANs combined with port-based ACLs
MACsec with downlink encryption and ISE authorization
questions.explanation: TrustSec assigns an SGT to each authenticated session at ingress via ISE authorization. The tag is propagated inline or via SXP, and egress devices apply SGACLs (source-SGT to destination-SGT matrices). This decouples policy from IP addresses and VLANs. MACsec provides link encryption, not segmentation.

questions.question: An engineer observes that a Cisco Secure Firewall (FTD) managed by FMC is blocking legitimate HTTPS traffic to a business partner site because SSL decryption cannot inspect it. The partner uses certificate pinning. What is the correct action?
options: Import the partner's private key into FMC to enable decryption
Create a Do Not Decrypt rule matching the partner domain in the SSL policy
Switch the decryption policy from Decrypt-Resign to Decrypt-Known-Key
Disable the SSL policy entirely on the affected access control rule
questions.explanation: Pinned applications reject any certificate not matching the exact pinned copy, so Decrypt-Resign breaks them. The supported approach is to add a Do Not Decrypt rule for the specific destination (URL category, SNI, or application) while keeping decryption enabled globally. Importing a private key is not possible (you do not own the partner's), and disabling the SSL policy is too broad.

questions.question: A security team is rolling out Cisco Umbrella as the primary DNS-layer security control. The CISO requires that users on managed corporate laptops receive granular, user-level policies even when off the corporate network. Which deployment method meets this requirement?
options: Deploy Umbrella Virtual Appliances (VAs) in each branch to forward DNS
Point internal DNS forwarders to the Umbrella resolvers using Cisco Secure Network conditional forwarding
Configure DHCP to push Umbrella resolvers 208.67.222.222 and 208.67.220.220
Install the Cisco Umbrella Roaming Client or AnyConnect Umbrella module on endpoints
questions.explanation: DHCP-based and VA-based deployments only work while on the corporate network and identify devices at the network level. The Umbrella Roaming Client (standalone or as an AnyConnect module) follows the device everywhere, encrypts DNS to Umbrella, and supports granular user/identity-based policies off-network.

questions.question: A developer integrates a third-party application with Cisco FMC using the REST API. The application retrieves access control rules every 30 seconds. After a week, the requests start failing with HTTP 429. What is the most likely cause?
options: The API token has expired; generate a new authentication token
The client is missing the Content-Type: application/json header
The FMC is rate-limiting the client because polling frequency exceeds
The FMC REST API requires re-authentication every 1000 calls
questions.explanation: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests indicates rate limiting. FMC caps REST API calls (typically 120 messages per minute per client/IP). Reducing polling frequency, using subscription-based mechanisms, or spacing calls fixes the issue. Expired tokens return 401, missing headers return 415.

questions.question: A manufacturing company uses Cisco Stealthwatch (Secure Network Analytics) to detect anomalous behavior. Analysts want to identify lateral movement where an internal host suddenly starts communicating with many internal hosts on uncommon ports. Which Stealthwatch feature best detects this?
options: Custom Security Events matching specific SGT flows
Behavioral algorithms on the High Concern Index with
Encrypted Traffic Analytics (ETA) for TLS visibility
Host Lock violations configured per host group
questions.explanation: Stealthwatch baselines normal east-west traffic patterns per host and raises the Concern Index when behavior deviates significantly, such as scanning many internal peers. ETA is for malware-in-encrypted-traffic, not lateral movement patterns, and Host Lock is a static policy violation mechanism.

questions.question: An engineer must enforce posture compliance so that only laptops with up-to-date Windows patches and a running AV agent can access corporate resources. Non-compliant devices receive remediation resources. Which Cisco ISE feature provides this?
options: Cisco ISE Posture Assessment using the AnyConnect
Cisco ISE Guest Services with sponsored access
Cisco ISE Profiling with DHCP/SNMP probes
questions.explanation: The ISE Posture Module (inside AnyConnect/Secure Client) evaluates the endpoint against posture policies. Non-compliant devices are given a restricted dACL and URL redirect to a remediation portal (patch server, AV update). Profiling identifies devices, it does not remediate them.

questions.question: A company's Cisco Secure Email (ESA) is receiving a spike in spoofed messages claiming to be from the CEO. The domain has SPF published but many messages still reach the inbox. What additional email authentication mechanism should be deployed and enforced?
options: Enable Sender IP Reputation (SBRS) to block low-reputation senders
Enable Graymail detection and safe unsubscribe
Use Forged Email Detection with a custom dictionary only
Configure DMARC with a reject policy in DNS.
questions.explanation: SPF alone only validates the envelope return-path; attackers can still spoof the From header. DMARC aligns SPF or DKIM with the From header and instructs receivers to reject non-aligned mail when p=reject is published. The ESA must also be configured to verify DMARC for inbound mail. combined with DKIM signing, and enable DMARC verification on the ESA

questions.question: A SOC analyst investigates a malware detection on an endpoint reported by Cisco Secure Endpoint. They need to see every file the process executed and every network connection it made, across time. Which Secure Endpoint feature provides this timeline?
options: Prevalence widget on the SecureX ribbon
questions.explanation: Device Trajectory shows a chronological process/file/network activity timeline for a specific host, while File Trajectory tracks where a specific SHA-256 was seen across the estate. Both together are essential for investigating scope and root cause. Retrospection re-evaluates past convictions when disposition changes.

questions.question: An engineer configures a Cisco ASA running multiple context mode. Which statement is correct about the admin context?
options: Any context can be designated as admin context and is used to access the system execution space and other contexts via changeto context
The admin context only stores licensing and cannot pass traffic
The admin context must be transparent mode
The admin context is used for system-wide administration such as file access and failover, and its configuration is always stored in the startup-config partition
questions.explanation: In multi-context ASA, you designate one user-created context as the admin context. From it, administrators log in and use changeto context to manage other contexts. It can also pass traffic like any other context. Mode (routed/transparent) is independent per context.

questions.question: A company uses a private Cisco PKI for issuing certificates to VPN users. Employees who leave must have their certificates invalidated immediately. Which PKI component provides near-real-time revocation validation without downloading large files?
options: SCEP auto-enrollment with short certificate lifetimes
Key Recovery Agent (KRA) holding copies of private keys
questions.explanation: OCSP lets a verifier query the current status of a single certificate in real time, avoiding the latency and size of downloading entire CRLs. SCEP is for enrollment, not revocation. Short lifetimes reduce window but do not provide immediate revocation.

questions.question: A security architect is choosing an IPsec IKEv2 proposal. The traffic is high-throughput east-west between two data centers and must use authenticated encryption to avoid separate HMAC processing. Which algorithm combination should be selected?
questions.explanation: AES-GCM is authenticated encryption: confidentiality and integrity are produced in a single pass, which is faster at high throughput than CBC+HMAC. DH group 20 (ECP-384) matches the 256-bit cipher strength, and PRF SHA-384 pairs with it. 3DES and DH groups 2/5 are deprecated; ChaCha20-Poly1305 is not yet a standard IKEv2 suite on most Cisco platforms.

questions.question: A DevSecOps team wants to catch vulnerable dependencies and insecure code patterns before the application is built and deployed. Which practice implements this shift-left principle?
options: Runtime application self-protection (RASP) agents installed at production
Periodic DAST scans against the production web application
SAST (Static Application Security Testing) and Software Composition
questions.explanation: Shift-left means finding defects as early as possible. SAST analyzes source code for insecure patterns, and SCA inspects dependency manifests (package-lock, pom.xml) for known CVEs. Running both automatically on every PR blocks vulnerable code from being merged. DAST, RASP, and pentests are valuable but later in the lifecycle.

questions.question: A Cisco Secure Web Appliance (WSA) is deployed in explicit proxy mode. Users report that after enabling HTTPS decryption, certain banking and payroll sites present a browser certificate error. What is the correct remediation?
options: Disable HTTPS decryption globally and rely on URL categorization only
Switch from explicit to transparent WCCP mode so certificates are not rewritten
Regenerate the root CA on the WSA every 24 hours
Install the WSA's self-signed HTTPS proxy certificate into the browser trust
questions.explanation: When the WSA decrypts TLS, it presents a certificate signed by its own CA. Browsers must trust that CA (pushed via GPO). For regulated/pinned sites (banking, payroll), a pass-through decryption policy avoids re-signing. Transparent mode does not change certificate behavior.

questions.question: An engineer deploys Cisco Umbrella SIG for a remote branch. They want web traffic to be inspected by the cloud firewall and forwarded securely from the branch router. Which tunnel type should be configured on the ISR?
options: DMVPN Phase 3 spoke tunnel toward a hub ASA
questions.explanation: Umbrella SIG supports IPsec IKEv2 tunnels from network devices (ISR, Meraki, etc.) to its cloud headends. Traffic is then inspected by Cloud-Delivered Firewall and secure web gateway. DMVPN, GETVPN, and L2TPv3 are not Umbrella SIG ingress methods.

questions.question: A Cisco ISE administrator wants non-compliant devices to be automatically quarantined and later released once remediated, without requiring manual session termination. Which RADIUS mechanism makes the switch terminate the session and re-authenticate the endpoint?
options: SNMP traps to the switch to bounce the port
questions.explanation: RFC 5176 RADIUS CoA lets ISE push a reauthentication or session termination to the NAS in real time. ISE uses this to dynamically enforce policy changes, such as moving a posture-violating endpoint into a restricted VLAN/dACL and back when remediated.

questions.question: A healthcare company stores PHI in an AWS S3 bucket. They must ensure data is encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys and that access is restricted to specific IAM roles. Which AWS configuration meets these requirements?
options: Enable SSE-S3 server-side encryption and allow public read with a bucket policy
Enable SSE-KMS with a customer-managed KMS key and restrict access with an IAM role +
Rely on TLS 1.2 in transit; S3 encrypts everything by default
Use client-side encryption with a static key stored in the application config
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer-managed CMK gives the customer control over key policy, rotation, and audit via CloudTrail. Combining it with an IAM role and a bucket policy referencing the role ARN ensures only authorized identities can decrypt. Public access contradicts PHI protection; hard-coded static keys are bad practice.

questions.question: An engineer enables NetFlow on a Cisco Catalyst switch to feed Stealthwatch. Which NetFlow version exports variable-length templates allowing Layer 2 fields, MAC addresses, and application identifiers?
questions.explanation: NetFlow v5 has a fixed record format and only IPv4 Layer 3 fields. NetFlow v9 introduced templates, making it extensible; IPFIX is its IETF standard. Both support Layer 2 MAC, IPv6, NBAR2 application IDs, and custom fields, which Stealthwatch consumes.

questions.question: A Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) generates an intrusion event for a Snort rule. The SOC wants to automatically query Cisco Threat Response/SecureX and see the reputation of the source IP, file hashes, and related incidents. Which integration enables this pivot?
questions.explanation: SecureX Threat Response aggregates context from multiple Cisco modules (Secure Endpoint, Umbrella, FMC, Email, Talos) and lets analysts pivot on observables (IP, hash, URL) with one click. The ribbon is the browser widget that surfaces this across product consoles.

questions.question: A security engineer is designing SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) between ISE and an older Catalyst switch that does not support inline SGT tagging. Which statement about SXP is correct?
options: SXP carries IP-to-SGT bindings over TCP.
SXP is a multicast protocol that floods SGT bindings to all devices
SXP uses UDP 4500 and requires IPsec for confidentiality
SXP can only run between ISE and Cisco ISR, not Catalyst switches
questions.explanation: SXP is a TCP-based protocol (default port 64999) that propagates IP-to-SGT bindings from tagging-capable devices (or ISE) to devices that cannot propagate tags inline. Speakers send bindings; Listeners receive and program their enforcement tables. allowing devices without inline tagging support to learn tags for enforcement

questions.question: A CIO is evaluating Cisco Secure Workload (Tetration). Which primary security benefit does it provide beyond traditional perimeter firewalls?
options: Automatic WAN link optimization between data centers
Certificate lifecycle management for web servers
Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) scrubbing at the edge
questions.explanation: Secure Workload collects telemetry from agents on every workload, discovers application dependencies, then generates and enforces microsegmentation policies (allow-list) at the host level. It works identically on bare metal, VMs, containers, AWS, Azure, and GCP. It is not a WAN optimizer or DDoS scrubber.

questions.question: An engineer troubleshoots an IKEv2 site-to-site VPN stuck in MM_WAIT_MSG2. Both peers have matching proposals, PSKs, and reachable IPs. Which is the most likely cause?
options: The ISAKMP authentication method is set to rsa-sig on one peer
The crypto ACLs on the two sides have overlapping subnets
Outbound UDP 500 or UDP 4500 is blocked or NAT is rewriting the
Mismatched IKEv2 lifetime values between peers
questions.explanation: MM_WAIT_MSG2 in the phase-1 state machine means the initiator is waiting for the first response from the peer. The overwhelming cause is Layer 3/4: UDP 500 (or 4500 with NAT-T) is dropped by a firewall or NAT without NAT-T. Proposal, PSK, and ACL mismatches appear in later states.

questions.question: A company wants to allow contractors temporary wireless access via a self-registration portal that emails a one-time password. Which ISE feature implements this?
options: BYOD portal with EAP-TLS certificate enrollment
questions.explanation: The ISE Self-Registered Guest Portal lets visitors create an account, optionally approved by a sponsor, and delivers credentials via email/SMS. The BYOD, Posture, and MyDevices portals serve different purposes (certificate provisioning, compliance checking, device lifecycle).

questions.question: A penetration tester gains access to a VLAN through a vulnerable kiosk and sends double-tagged 802.1Q frames hoping to reach a protected VLAN. Which mitigation specifically prevents this VLAN hopping attack?
options: Assign native VLAN to the same VLAN as a data VLAN on trunks
Disable DTP and set access ports to switchport
Enable BPDU Guard on all access ports
questions.explanation: Double-tagging attacks work when the native VLAN on a trunk is used by normal access ports and when DTP allows unsolicited trunk negotiation. Hardcoding access ports, disabling DTP, using a dedicated unused native VLAN, and tagging it with vlan dot1q tag native prevent the attack. plus assign a dedicated unused native VLAN on trunks and tag native VLANs

questions.question: A Cisco Umbrella Investigate analyst notices a domain with a high risk score, recent registration, and fast-flux DNS. Which characteristic is the strongest indicator that this domain is likely used for malware C2?
options: The domain uses Let's Encrypt certificates
Short TTL DNS records with rapidly rotating IPs
The domain is registered with a privacy proxy
The domain has HTTPS enabled with TLS 1.3
questions.explanation: Fast-flux DNS (very short TTL, IPs changing quickly across many ASNs) combined with a brand-new registration is a strong malware/botnet C2 signal. Let's Encrypt and WHOIS privacy are common on benign sites and are weak indicators on their own.

questions.question: An engineer configures Cisco AnyConnect (Secure Client) remote access VPN on an ASA. Which feature steers only corporate subnets through the tunnel while sending Internet-bound traffic directly?
questions.explanation: Split tunneling with an include ACL (tunnelspecified) pushes only the listed subnets down the VPN, while everything else uses the client's local Internet. Hair-pinning is used for client-to-client traffic through the same ASA interface, not for Internet offload.

questions.question: A Cisco Secure Email Gateway is configured with Advanced Malware Protection (AMP). A user reports that a file delivered yesterday is now being flagged as malicious. Which AMP capability is responsible for detecting previously-delivered malicious files after disposition changes?
options: File Reputation at the moment of delivery
questions.explanation: AMP continuously re-evaluates file dispositions. If a file originally marked clean is later judged malicious (through sandboxing or Talos intel), Retrospective Detection fires alerts and allows administrators to identify previously delivered copies across mail and endpoints.

questions.question: An engineer configures OSPF authentication between two Cisco routers. The security team requires strong integrity and replay protection rather than plain MD5. Which option should be configured?
options: Authentication using a key chain with
questions.explanation: Modern IOS/IOS-XE supports HMAC-SHA cryptographic authentication for OSPF using key chains with rotation and lifetimes. Legacy MD5 is still available but weaker. BGP-style neighbor password and null authentication are unrelated.

questions.question: A CASB product (Cisco Cloudlock) flags that several employees uploaded sensitive CRM records to an unsanctioned third-party SaaS. Which cloud security concept does Cloudlock address?
questions.explanation: CASBs inspect SaaS activity via API and inline modes: they discover Shadow IT, classify data (DLP), and apply policy against unsanctioned or risky sharing. Cloudlock integrates with Salesforce, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, etc. It is not a DNS or K8s tool.

questions.question: A corporate policy states that privileged network device administrators must authenticate with MFA and have their commands audited. Which protocol provides command-by-command authorization and accounting?
questions.explanation: TACACS+ separates authentication, authorization, and accounting and can authorize each individual command and log it. RADIUS authorizes the session as a whole, not per command. ISE supports TACACS+ with device admin licensing to provide per-command MFA and audit.

questions.question: An architect is choosing between Cisco DMVPN and GETVPN for a large multi-site MPLS backbone where all sites must freely reach each other and encryption must preserve original source/destination addresses for multicast routing. Which technology fits best?
questions.explanation: GETVPN uses group keys distributed by a Key Server via GDOI. Because it does not tunnel-encapsulate, the original IP header is preserved, which lets MPLS routing and multicast work natively across the encrypted overlay. DMVPN/FlexVPN tunnel the traffic, changing outer headers.

questions.question: Security Operations wants to detect malware in encrypted TLS traffic without decrypting it. Which Cisco capability uses metadata such as initial data packet, sequence of packet lengths and times, and byte distribution to make this judgment?
questions.explanation: ETA exports enhanced NetFlow with IDP (initial data packet), SPLT (sequence of packet lengths and times), and byte distribution. Stealthwatch + Cognitive Analytics + Talos build ML models that detect known malware families without breaking encryption.

questions.question: An engineer is configuring a Cisco Secure Firewall access control policy. A rule must inspect traffic for intrusions using a balanced Snort ruleset and also log connections. What rule action must be used?
questions.explanation: The Allow action passes traffic through the AC rule while letting attached inspection (intrusion, file, variable set) run on it. Trust bypasses inspection. Monitor is passive and cannot be terminal. Block prevents traffic entirely.

questions.question: An analyst investigates suspicious PowerShell activity on a Windows endpoint using Cisco Secure Endpoint. They want to isolate the host from the network but keep communication with Secure Endpoint cloud for investigation. Which feature provides this?
questions.explanation: Secure Endpoint's Host Isolation quarantines an endpoint by blocking all network traffic except the connector's communication back to the cloud, allowing forensics without leaking lateral movement. It can be released remotely once the threat is contained.

questions.question: An organization wants NTP to be authenticated between routers to prevent an attacker from spoofing time and forging log timestamps. Which configuration is correct?
questions.explanation: NTP authentication requires defining a shared key (ntp authentication-key), enabling authentication (ntp authenticate), marking the key as trusted (ntp trusted-key), and binding it on the server statement. Without all four, messages will not be authenticated. ntp authenticate, and ntp trusted-key on both devices, then reference the key on the ntp server command

questions.question: A security engineer wants an AAA design where the same policy server provides RADIUS for wireless users, 802.1X for wired users, TACACS+ for device admin, and posture checks. Which Cisco product covers all of these in one platform?
questions.explanation: ISE supersedes ACS and supports RADIUS, 802.1X/EAP, posture, profiling, and TACACS+ (via Device Admin license). A single policy server simplifies policy and reporting. NPS and FreeRADIUS do not provide TACACS+ device admin or posture natively.

questions.question: An engineer configures a Cisco ASA for Active/Standby failover. Which requirement must be met for stateful failover to preserve existing TCP sessions during a failover event?
options: Stateful failover only works in multi-context routed mode
Both units must run different software versions to avoid simultaneous bugs
A dedicated stateful failover link (or sharing the failover link) with
One unit in routed mode and the other in transparent mode
questions.explanation: Stateful failover replicates the connection table between units over a stateful link (dedicated or shared with the failover link). Both units must have identical hardware, modules, software versions, and licenses. Mixed modes or versions break failover.

questions.question: A global enterprise wants to consolidate WAN, SD-WAN, SWG, CASB, ZTNA, and FWaaS into one cloud-delivered offering that follows the user — not the data centre. Branch sites and roaming users connect to the nearest cloud PoP, which enforces a single policy. Which architecture does Gartner call this?
options: Software-Defined Perimeter (SDP) — restricted to identity-based dark-cloud access for individual apps; not a converged WAN-plus-security stack
Cisco DNA Center — campus and SD-Access management plane; not a converged cloud-edge architecture
ACI Multi-Site Orchestrator — fabric-level orchestration for data-centre ACI, not a WAN/SaaS edge framework
questions.explanation: SASE, coined by Gartner, converges WAN (SD-WAN) and network security as a cloud service: SWG, CASB, ZTNA, FWaaS, DNS. Cisco's stack delivers this via Umbrella SIG, Catalyst SD-WAN, and Duo ZTNA. It is not a hardware product or a compliance standard. CASB, ZTNA, FWaaS, DNS security); Cisco delivers it via Umbrella SIG, Catalyst SD-WAN, and Duo

questions.question: A security analyst wants to automate incident response: when Cisco Secure Endpoint detects malware, Umbrella should add the associated domain to a block list, and an investigation ticket should be opened. Which Cisco platform orchestrates multi-product workflows like this?
questions.explanation: SecureX Orchestration provides drag-and-drop workflows (atomic actions, HTTP requests, logic) that pivot between Secure Endpoint, Umbrella, FMC, Email, Threat Response, ServiceNow, and more. Catalyst Center and Prime focus on network management, not security SOAR.

questions.question: A company evaluates authenticated API access for partners calling its gateway. Which mechanism provides scoped, expiring access tokens and is widely recommended for REST API authentication?
options: OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens with scopes and
Basic Auth over HTTPS with a shared static password
API keys hardcoded into the client
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 grants scoped, time-bound bearer tokens, supporting rotation and revocation. Static passwords/keys are long-lived secrets that leak easily. Mutual TLS alone cannot express fine-grained scopes. The best practice for modern APIs is OAuth plus mTLS for strong mutual auth. ideally combined with mTLS for machine-to-machine

questions.question: A malicious actor is performing a MAC flooding attack against an access switch, causing the CAM table to overflow so that the switch fails open and floods frames. Which mitigation stops this attack?
options: Set spanning-tree portfast on access ports
questions.explanation: Port-security caps the number of distinct source MACs learned on an access port. When exceeded, the port is restricted or shutdown, preventing the CAM overflow that makes a switch flood frames. DHCP snooping addresses a different attack vector.

questions.question: A forensic team investigates an insider threat. They need to correlate user login events with network flows and file access from weeks ago. Which Cisco capability stores enriched session context linking username to IP address over time?
options: ASA NetFlow Secure Event Logging (NSEL) without pxGrid
questions.explanation: pxGrid is Cisco's Platform Exchange Grid: ISE publishes session context (username, SGT, device type, posture) and subscribers like Stealthwatch, FMC, Secure Endpoint consume it to attribute flows and events to identity, enabling historical user-centric investigation.

questions.question: An engineer must decide between Cisco AnyConnect SSL VPN and IPsec IKEv2 remote access. Remote users are often behind hotel NAT and restrictive firewalls that only allow HTTP/HTTPS. Which option is most likely to succeed in all locations?
options: IKEv2 on UDP 500 with no NAT-T
questions.explanation: SSL VPN over TCP 443 looks like normal HTTPS and traverses almost any NAT or captive portal. DTLS on UDP 443 accelerates once available. IKEv1/IKEv2 over UDP 500/4500 is frequently blocked in guest/hotel networks.

questions.question: A security architect is briefing leadership on a model that assumes the network is compromised by default, treats every request as untrusted regardless of network origin, and verifies identity + device posture + context on every access decision. The model relies on dynamic policy rather than a static perimeter. Which statement about this architecture is accurate?
options: It assumes the corporate network is trusted by default and applies controls only at the perimeter, between the internal and external networks
It is a network architecture that assumes no implicit trust based on network location and continuously verifies every request using identity, device posture, and
It is a synonym for micro-segmentation; the term refers exclusively to east-west firewalling between workloads in the same data centre
It is a Cisco-specific product family delivered solely through ISE and Secure Firewall and not implementable with other vendor stacks
questions.explanation: NIST SP 800-207 defines Zero Trust around three tenets: verify explicitly (identity, device, context), use least-privileged access, and assume breach. Network location is not a trust anchor, and encryption remains essential. continuously verifies every access request, and enforces least privilege regardless of network location

questions.question: A Snort 3 rule on Cisco Secure Firewall reads: `alert http any any -> any any (msg:"admin path"; http_uri; content:"admin"; sid:1000001;)`. The author is restricting where the content match must appear. Which statement best describes the effect of the `http_uri` modifier in this rule?
options: It restricts the `content` match to the HTTP URI buffer (path + query) only — packets matching `admin` elsewhere (headers, body) are NOT flagged
It applies the content match to every HTTP header except the URI, the opposite of what the keyword name suggests
It enables URI normalisation but does not constrain where the content match is applied within the HTTP message
It activates rule action `block` for any URI containing the string, regardless of where in the URI it appears, and bypasses normalisation
questions.explanation: Snort 3 introduced buffers (http_uri, http_header, http_client_body, etc.) that isolate where content matching is applied. http_uri limits the match to the normalized request URI, preventing false positives from payload elsewhere.

questions.question: A container security engineer wants to ensure that only signed images from an approved registry can be deployed to a Kubernetes cluster. Which mechanism enforces this at admission time?
options: Pod Security Admission labels on namespaces (without additional verification)
A Kubernetes NetworkPolicy denying egress to unknown registries
RBAC ClusterRole limiting who can use kubectl apply
questions.explanation: Admission controllers validate objects before they are persisted. OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno policies can require images to come from an approved registry and pass cosign signature verification. PSA handles pod security standards, not image provenance. questions.question: A Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) deployment must block outbound connections to newly registered domains (NRDs) often associated with phishing. Which feature achieves this without maintaining a manual list?
options: NAT rule with destination zone any
questions.explanation: Security Intelligence uses Talos-maintained feeds (malware, phishing, botnets, NRD, DGA) to block, monitor, or allow traffic by IP/URL/DNS reputation before the access control rules fire. It is updated automatically.

questions.question: A cloud team must ensure that EC2 instances cannot reach the Internet but can call AWS services privately. Which configuration meets this?
options: VPC Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) for required AWS services and no
Route table with default route to a Transit Gateway toward an on-prem proxy
Public subnet with an Elastic IP and stateful NACL
Security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 outbound and a NAT Gateway
questions.explanation: VPC endpoints (Gateway for S3/DynamoDB, Interface/PrivateLink for most others) route traffic to AWS services over the AWS private backbone without crossing the Internet. Removing the IGW route ensures the subnet is truly private.

questions.question: An engineer wants to encrypt a flash disk image backup using strong symmetric encryption. Which algorithm offers the best balance of security and performance for 2026-era hardware with AES-NI?
questions.explanation: AES-256-GCM provides authenticated encryption (confidentiality + integrity) and is hardware-accelerated by AES-NI, making it both fast and secure. DES, RC4, and Blowfish are legacy or weak and should not be used for new designs.

questions.question: An ISE administrator configures a policy where machine authentication must succeed before user authentication is allowed (so only corporate-joined devices can get user access). Which EAP feature provides this?
questions.explanation: EAP chaining (originally EAP-FAST, now TEAP in modern deployments) authenticates both machine and user in a single exchange and ties them together so ISE can enforce 'domain-joined device AND valid user' policies. PEAP/MS-CHAPv2 cannot chain identities.

questions.question: An engineer deploys FlexVPN on a hub-spoke topology using IKEv2. Which feature allows spokes to dynamically build spoke-to-spoke tunnels on demand using shortcut switching?
options: IKEv1 aggressive mode with wildcard PSK
questions.explanation: FlexVPN supports NHRP redirect/shortcut similar to DMVPN Phase 3, allowing the hub to redirect spokes to each other. Spokes then establish direct on-demand tunnels without hair-pinning through the hub.

questions.question: A Cisco ESA administrator needs to prevent users from seeing marketing or promotional mail in their inboxes while still letting them opt out. Which ESA capability provides this?
options: Content Filter with quarantine action for all .html mail
questions.explanation: Graymail detection classifies legitimate bulk mail (marketing, social, bulk) and can move it out of the inbox. Safe Unsubscribe lets users opt out via a proxy that protects them from malicious unsubscribe links. FED detects CEO impersonation, not graymail.

questions.question: A corporate policy requires that laptops be automatically enrolled with a client certificate used for 802.1X EAP-TLS when joining the network for the first time. Which ISE workflow accomplishes this?
options: BYOD onboarding portal with Cisco ISE
Device Administration portal with TACACS+ authorization
questions.explanation: The BYOD/Onboarding flow uses a provisioning portal that installs a certificate profile. ISE can act as its own internal CA or forward requests via SCEP to Microsoft NDES/ADCS. The device then uses EAP-TLS with that cert for ongoing authentication.

questions.question: A security engineer wants to prevent IP address spoofing at the edge of the network so that attackers cannot forge source addresses from inside routed segments. Which IOS feature accomplishes this at the interface level?
questions.explanation: Strict-mode uRPF accepts a packet only if the source address is reachable via the interface it came in on (symmetric path). This blocks spoofed packets at the edge (BCP 38). CoPP protects the control plane; port-security is Layer 2.

questions.question: An engineer designs a Secure Internet access for branch offices. Umbrella SIG policy must apply per user identity. Which integration makes Umbrella cloud firewall and SWG aware of user identities from Active Directory?
options: SNMP polling of the domain controller
questions.explanation: Umbrella AD Connector pushes user-to-IP mappings from domain controllers so that Umbrella policies in-network can be user-scoped; for roaming users, the AnyConnect Umbrella/SWG module signs requests with identity. Neither RC nor VA alone provides AD user identity.

questions.question: A forensic engineer must validate the integrity of a captured disk image against its original. Which cryptographic function is most appropriate to produce a collision-resistant fingerprint in 2026?
questions.explanation: MD5 and SHA-1 have practical collision attacks and are no longer considered collision-resistant. CRC32 is an error-detection code, not a cryptographic hash. SHA-256 (SHA-2) or SHA-3 are the current standards for forensic integrity hashing. recommended)
